body:
## Purpose

This PR extends the operator broadcasting API from #2598 to finite difference operators, completing the finite difference phase of #2468. A finite difference operator is now an ordinary `Broadcasted` that is applied one column at a time through `apply_operator`, using the `foreach_slice` loops from #2522 and #2571, so that finite difference and spectral element operators share one implementation of fusion on CPUs and GPUs, and the CUDA extension no longer contains any finite difference code. On GPUs, every argument that an operator reads at neighboring points is computed once per point, and slices that fit in a warp keep these values in registers and read them with warp shuffles.

## Disclosure

The second commit and description of this PR were mostly generated using Claude.

## Content

- One broadcast API for spectral element and finite difference operators
  - An operator broadcast's `copyto!` runs one `foreach_slice` loop over slabs or columns, applying each slice with `apply_operator`.
  - Nested finite difference operators are evaluated in a single pass over each column whenever possible; intermediate results stay in registers.
  - The CUDA extension has no more finite difference kernels; `CLIMA_FD_MAX_THREADS` and `Operators.getidx` are removed.
  - Operators check the spaces of their arguments and destinations: arguments or destinations with the wrong staggering, other levels or other horizontal spaces throw a `DimensionMismatch`, while columns of the same space are broadcast against it.
  - Column operations support `MultiColumnSpace`s, 1-D extruded spaces, and slab and column fields.
- Linear operators as band matrix products
  - Linear finite difference operators are products with their band matrices (`FDOperatorMatrix`), shared with `MatrixFields` products.
  - Boundary rows are clipped interior rows, and advection stencils extrapolate ghost points at clamped indices, so operators need no boundary stencils, except for the `SetValue` stencils of `GradientC2F`, `DivergenceC2F`, `CurlC2F` and `UpwindBiasedProductC2F`.
  - These `SetValue` stencils read the closest center of the argument that the operator already reads, so they never materialize lazy arguments (or, on GPUs, read the registers of other threads). The constructors of these operators no longer return a `DirichletOperator`, which is only kept for backward compatibility.
  - The second operand of a product is projected once per point; cheap pointwise operands are recomputed rather than cached.
  - Band products read the bands inside the column without branching on each entry.
- Operator arguments cached once per point
  - On GPUs, arguments read at other points are computed once, by the thread owning the point, before the enclosing expression is evaluated.
  - Slices that fit in a warp keep these arguments in registers read with warp shuffles (`ShuffledArray`); larger slices use shared buffers, synchronized only before passes that read them.
  - Arguments read only at a thread's own points are evaluated once into registers.
  - Register temporaries of `foreach_slice` loop bodies are frozen into `SArray`s before operators read them, and they are always cached, since other threads cannot read them; only lazy arguments whose buffers would need too much shared memory are recomputed instead. CPU scopes have no buffer limit.
- Bug fixes
  - A boundary value that varies along the column is read at its first level on the bottom boundary and its last on the top; `main` read the first on both.
  - `CurlC2F` has the `Contravariant12Vector` element type it computes; `main` declared `Contravariant123Vector`.
  - A vector boundary value imposed on a `NamedTuple` of fluxes applies to every component; `main` failed to compile this on GPUs.
  - `.&&` and `.||` are compatible with `Grids.toggle_placeholder_grid`; `main` failed to `adapt` the closures created by `AndAnd` and `OrOr` from `Base.Broadcasted`.
  - Linear operators in the lazy inputs of column reductions are applied as band matrix products (`main` evaluates them through boxed device calls).
  - Extrapolation weights are always floats, since the NVPTX backend of LLVM 15 appears to have a bug that negates runtime integer-to-float conversions.
  - The CUDA extension compiles with both CUDA.jl v5 and v6; `main` could not compile with v6.
- GPU addressing
  - Point index arithmetic is 32-bit: `UInt32` thread ranks and slice ranges, 32-bit view offsets and strides, `DevicePointView`s instead of `SubArray`s.
  - Kernels receive views of device arrays as compact views and assume the extents fixed by a layout's type (checked at launch), so offsets fold into constant strides.
  - GPU kernels support at most 2^32 - 1 elements per array and 2^31 - 1 slices per `foreach_slice` loop.
- Launch overhead and compile latency
  - A CUDA launch converts its arguments and compiles its kernel once; launch configurations are cached by kernel handle, and one-thread-per-column kernels are spread over every multiprocessor.
  - The thread-pool launch is inferred once for all loop bodies, pointwise stencil nodes are read through a generated method, and privately buffered columns enter their point loop directly.
  - Slice values are read through their parent arrays with one linear index per value, and internal slicing skips user-level checks.
  - The shared memory estimate that decides whether nested operator applications are inlined does not charge arguments that stay in registers.
- Other simplifications
  - Product and quotient types are inferred with `Utilities.return_type` instead of a duplicate implementation; `mul_return_type` and `inv_return_type` are removed.
  - Lazy operator matrices are materialized with `Fields.shared_space` instead of a duplicate implementation.

## Comparison against main

All comparisons are against `main` at [061753f02](https://github.com/CliMA/ClimaCore.jl/commit/061753f022e99eb26551dc4548eb5b6bfda37d65), the last commit before this PR was merged.

Each row compares this PR with `main` ([7992](https://buildkite.com/clima/climacore-ci/builds/7992) for the last PR merged into main, [499](https://buildkite.com/clima/climacore-end-to-end-performance/builds/499) with the Makie pin of this PR's perf pipeline, and [452](https://buildkite.com/clima/climaatmos-downstream/builds/452) with CUDA pinned to 5.11.3) over the jobs or benchmark cases that passed in both builds on the same hardware, setup jobs excluded. Rows over several jobs or cases give the min / median / max of the PR values, `main` values, and per-job ratios; the CPU benchmark jobs ran on different node types than `main`'s and are left out.

| Performance metrics | PR | `main` | PR vs `main` | Num values | Build IDs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Run-time allocations per job | 52 / 33260 / 83849 allocs | 53 / 49520 / 121455 allocs | -53% / -31% / -2% | 5 | [8015](https://buildkite.com/clima/climacore-ci/builds/8015), [449](https://buildkite.com/clima/climaatmos-downstream/builds/449) |
| GPU FD operator benchmark time per call, P100 | 14 / 206 / 1246 µs | 16 / 498 / 1988 µs | -80% / -50% / +28% | 133 | [8015](https://buildkite.com/clima/climacore-ci/builds/8015) |
| ClimaAtmos wall time per simulated year | 0.000172 / 1.14 / 71.4 days | 0.000181 / 1.14 / 76.9 days | -34% / -3% / +86% | 49 | [449](https://buildkite.com/clima/climaatmos-downstream/builds/449) |
| Flagship AMIP wall time per simulated year | 2.54 days | 2.87 days | -12% | 1 | [503](https://buildkite.com/clima/climacore-end-to-end-performance/builds/503) |
| Wall time per simulation, global soil model (GPU) | 0.0975 s | 0.123 s | -21% | 1 | [503](https://buildkite.com/clima/climacore-end-to-end-performance/builds/503) |
| Wall time per simulation, snowy land model (GPU) | 0.247 s | 0.382 s | -35% | 1 | [503](https://buildkite.com/clima/climacore-end-to-end-performance/builds/503) |
| ClimaAtmos `step!` time, CPU aquaplanet | 16.018 s | 17.427 s | -8% | 1 | [449](https://buildkite.com/clima/climaatmos-downstream/builds/449) |
| ClimaAtmos `step!` time, GPU aquaplanet | 0.040 s | 0.080 s | -50% | 1 | [449](https://buildkite.com/clima/climaatmos-downstream/builds/449) |
| ClimaAtmos `step!` time, GPU prognostic EDMF | 0.080 s | 0.138 s | -42% | 1 | [449](https://buildkite.com/clima/climaatmos-downstream/builds/449) |

| Compilation metrics | PR | `main` | PR vs `main` | Num values | Build IDs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ClimaAtmos jobs, cache build time | 30 / 76 / 206 s | 33 / 72 / 224 s | -18% / -1% / +46% | 65 | [449](https://buildkite.com/clima/climaatmos-downstream/builds/449) |
| ClimaAtmos single-column prognostic EDMF jobs, cache build time | 53 / 98 / 206 s | 53 / 100 / 216 s | -17% / -2% / +12% | 19 | [449](https://buildkite.com/clima/climaatmos-downstream/builds/449) |
| ClimaAtmos jobs, cache build memory | 6.0 / 11.4 / 25.0 GiB | 6.4 / 11.4 / 25.8 GiB | -8% / -1% / +3% | 65 | [449](https://buildkite.com/clima/climaatmos-downstream/builds/449) |
| Flagship AMIP cache build time | 313 s | 290 s | +8% | 1 | [503](https://buildkite.com/clima/climacore-end-to-end-performance/builds/503) |
| Flagship AMIP cache build memory | 37.1 GiB | 39.3 GiB | -6% | 1 | [503](https://buildkite.com/clima/climacore-end-to-end-performance/builds/503) |

The downstream builds of this PR ([449](https://buildkite.com/clima/climaatmos-downstream/builds/449)) and of `main` ([452](https://buildkite.com/clima/climaatmos-downstream/builds/452)) ran the same ClimaAtmos (CliMA/ClimaAtmos.jl@352fe9846) and package versions, with CUDA pinned to 5.11.3 by temporary branches, since CUDA 6.4.1 roughly doubles the compilation time of the GPU jobs and `main`'s CUDA extension does not load with it. The perf builds ran after external package updates lowered `main`'s flagship AMIP SYPD from 0.363 (build [485](https://buildkite.com/clima/climacore-end-to-end-performance/builds/485)) to 0.348. The AMIP SYPD moves by about ±1% between builds, depending on whether the land benchmarks run alongside it. The ClimaAtmos CPU cases can vary by ±25% on the same node types, so their aggregate rows mostly reflect noise.

### Profiling results

The perf pipeline's land benchmarks profiled 3 steps of the land model on an A100 ([503](https://buildkite.com/clima/climacore-end-to-end-performance/builds/503) for this PR and [499](https://buildkite.com/clima/climacore-end-to-end-performance/builds/499) for `main`), and a temporary job of build [503](https://buildkite.com/clima/climacore-end-to-end-performance/builds/503#01a14928-875e-4b44-947c-9ff2e94b7bbd) profiled 20 flagship AMIP steps on an A100 with both this PR and `main`:

| Trace metric | PR | `main` | PR vs `main` |
|---|---|---|---|
| GPU idle fraction per snowy land model step | 31.7% | 57.6% | -45% |
| CUDA trace events per snowy land model step | 30301 | 49990 | -39% |
| GPU idle fraction per flagship AMIP step | 16.4% | 16.4% | +0% |
| CUDA trace events per flagship AMIP step | 104309 | 145211 | -28% |

The AMIP kernels of the two traces (641 each) take 194.1 and 220.4 ms of GPU time per step; they can be split into categories as follows:

| Kernel category | PR ms/step (share) | `main` ms/step (share) | PR vs `main` | Num kernels |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| pointwise | 82.38 (42.5%) | 89.59 (40.7%) | -8% | 409 |
| radiation (RRTMGP) | 55.14 (28.4%) | 56.87 (25.8%) | -3% | 17 |
| stencil | 33.68 (17.4%) | 39.40 (17.9%) | -15% | 139 |
| spectral | 10.36 (5.3%) | 20.30 (9.2%) | -49% | 33 |
| linear solve | 6.17 (3.2%) | 7.22 (3.3%) | -15% | 5 |
| DSS | 4.52 (2.3%) | 4.66 (2.1%) | -3% | 24 |
| column reduction | 0.70 (0.4%) | 0.97 (0.4%) | -28% | 6 |
| limiter | 0.55 (0.3%) | 0.78 (0.4%) | -29% | 3 |
| copy and fill | 0.56 (0.3%) | 0.56 (0.3%) | +0% | 5 |
| **all kernels** | **194.1 (100%)** | **220.4 (100%)** | **-12%** | 641 |

The stencil kernels, split by the number of levels in their outputs, by whether they multiply matrix fields, and by whether they contain nonlinear (advection) operators:

| Stencil kernel category | PR ms/step (share) | `main` ms/step (share) | PR vs `main` | Num kernels |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 63-level outputs (atmos) | 27.73 (14.3%) | 32.52 (14.8%) | -15% | 86 |
| 64-level outputs (atmos) | 5.36 (2.8%) | 5.99 (2.7%) | -10% | 39 |
| other outputs (land) | 0.59 (0.3%) | 0.90 (0.4%) | -34% | 14 |
| matrix multiplications | 18.17 (9.4%) | 20.36 (9.2%) | -11% | 71 |
| stencil applications | 15.50 (8.0%) | 19.04 (8.6%) | -19% | 68 |
| linear operators | 27.20 (14.0%) | 30.98 (14.1%) | -12% | 121 |
| nonlinear operators | 6.48 (3.3%) | 8.42 (3.8%) | -23% | 18 |
| **all stencil kernels** | **33.7 (17.4%)** | **39.4 (17.9%)** | **-15%** | 139 |
